Test a weighted combination using inverse_error weights to see if a data‑driven weighting improves over the robust trimmed mean, given the unstable ranking and strong trend/seasonality.
Test a softmax‑based weighting to see if a more aggressive weighting improves over trimmed mean, given the strong trend/seasonality and unstable ranking.
The series has unstable ranking (tau -0.045) and strong trend/seasonality, so a robust median might outperform trimmed mean.
Try a per‑horizon weighted mean using the top‑k per‑horizon handle w4, which may capture horizon‑specific strengths in this highly seasonal, trend‑dominated series.
test a simple mean combination on the full pool to see if the robust trimmed mean is indeed best; mean is a different kind of robustifier.
The series has unstable ranking (tau –0.045) and many correlated error groups; a per‑horizon top‑k mean may capture the best model at each horizon without overfitting.
The series has unstable ranking and high correlation groups; a weighted scheme that adapts to error trend across windows might better balance models that improve vs degrade.
The series has unstable ranking (tau -0.045) and strong trend/seasonality, so a robust DBA combination might improve over trimmed_mean.
The series shows unstable ranking and strong trend/seasonality, so a robust but potentially adaptive weighting like forward selection may capture complementary models.
Use per‑horizon best‑model weighting to capture horizon‑dependent dominance, addressing unstable ranking and strong seasonality.
Try a robust weighted combination on the small stable pool to see if a tighter subset improves SMAPE, given the unstable ranking and strong trend/seasonality.

decision.justification: Selected 'weighted weighted by w7' (an agent proposal) as the best of 12 backtested attempts, score 0.9617. Series context: trend strength 1.0 and seasonal strength 1.0; model ranking is unstable across windows (Kendall tau -0.045); 3 of 19 models carry independent error; relative error spread across the pool is 0.73.
